editorial:
Imagine moving back to your hometown to start over, only to find out your mom has a secret superpower. That is exactly what happens to Marion. She leaves her husband on their wedding day and moves back to Tyrol with her daughter, Laura. While Marion wants to be a professional doctor and run her father's clinic, her mother, Halfried, has a natural gift for healing people with her hands. The vibe is very cozy and emotional, focusing on a family trying to figure out how they fit together while dealing with the judgment of the local villagers who don't trust outsiders.

You will really enjoy the tension between the science-based medicine Marion uses and the magical healing her mother provides. The acting feels very real, though the story moves at a slower, more relaxed pace. It is a great pick if you like heart-warming stories about family bonds and secrets.
endingExplained: In the end, Marion finally stops fighting her mother and accepts that some things cannot be explained by science. She realizes that her daughter, Laura, also has the gift of healing. This discovery brings the three generations of women closer together. The family finds peace and balance, combining medical knowledge with natural gifts to help their community. Everyone learns to accept each other, and Marion finds her own happiness and strength in her hometown.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and stories about hidden gifts.
watchReasons: interesting mix of magic and science
